1931.text: Here 'I give thanks... churches... give thanks as well' sits squarely within the base gloss of grateful acknowledgment toward human benefactors who risked their lives — no notable divergence from the term's ordinary interpersonal-gratitude sense.

1932.text: G2168 co-occurs with 'life/soul' (M47, G5590H) and 'churches' (M44, G1577). Here thanksgiving is directed corporately (by Paul and 'all the churches') toward those who risked their own life/soul for another's sake — thanksgiving functions as the corporate, ongoing response owed to sacrificial risk-taking on behalf of the community.

1933.text: The role-T3 operation word 'risked' (G5294) is initiated by the unnamed persons (Prisca and Aquila) and directed toward saving 'my life' (Paul's) — the risking-act is the ground for the thanksgiving that follows, though G2168 itself carries no T3 tag in this verse.

2954.text: The large majority of G2168's occurrences (Rom.1.8; 1Cor.1.4; Eph.5.20; Col.1.3; 1Thess.5.18; Rev.11.17; 2Thess.2.13; Rom.16.4; 1Thess.2.13; 2Thess.1.3; 1Cor.1.14; 1Cor.14.18; Phil.1.3; 1Thess.1.2; Phlm.1.4; 1Cor.10.30; Col.1.12; 2Cor.1.11; Eph.1.16) share one core sense across the strong's own full occurrence list: an epistolary/liturgical, habitual first- or plural-person verb of thanking God, usually 'always'/'constantly' and grounded in some grace, faith, or benefit already received in the addressees or the speaker. This is the dominant register of the strong internally and forms the baseline against which the meal-blessing and single exceptional uses (below) stand out.

2956.text: Since G2168 is the subgroup's sole member strong, the cross-strong comparison this stage exists to perform collapses to a single-strong self-comparison: every occurrence -- whether epistolary-habitual, meal-blessing, exclamatory-nominal, negated, or personal/individual prayer-address -- shares the same root act (a verbal/enacted response of gratitude directed to God, occasionally to a human benefactor as in Rom.16.4) with no second lexeme to diverge from within this subgroup. The genuine internal variation is therefore register/context-driven (liturgical meal-formula vs. epistolary habit vs. individual prayer vs. negated failure) rather than lexical-sense divergence between two different words.

2990.text: The mode of operation varies by context: liturgical/formulaic over food (Matt.26.27, Mark.14.23, John.6.11), individual spoken prayer address (John.11.41, Luke.18.11), corporate liturgical address by heavenly beings (Rev.11.17), and continuous mental/epistolary habit ('always,' 'without ceasing') in apostolic letters (Col.1.3, Eph.1.16) -- direction is consistently human/creature-to-God (or occasionally human-to-human, Rom.16.4), and no differing constitutional level (spirit/soul/body) is distinguished in the evidence beyond the embodied posture in Luke.17.16.

2995.text: Thanksgiving operates somewhat differently within existing bonds versus across distance: within covenantal/familial-in-Christ bonds it is habitual and relational ('I thank my God always for you,' addressed to known brothers/churches), while directed toward God as ultimate benefactor it is vertical/devotional regardless of any human relational distance; a rare instance crosses ordinary social distance entirely when directed toward human benefactors who risked their lives (Rom.16.4), showing the characteristic can also operate horizontally toward a non-divine party.

2996.text: The characteristic crosses covenantal boundaries: while most occurrences are within the believing/covenant community (thanks for brothers' faith, election, sanctification), the Samaritan leper (Luke.17.16, explicitly noted as an outsider) and the Pharisee's misuse (Luke.18.11) show thanksgiving extended to or attempted by persons outside the immediate believing-covenant circle, and the human-directed thanks of Rom.16.4 crosses into ordinary interpersonal (non-covenantal-strictly) gratitude.

2997.text: The relational scope is broad in principle (any person, believer or outsider, may give thanks, and thanks may be directed to God or to a human benefactor) but the evidence shows it functionally clustered among believers thanking God for one another and, in one negative case, withheld by those who knew God but refused to honor him -- excluding, by that refusal, themselves from the fitting response rather than the characteristic itself excluding any class of person.

3009.text: Where thanksgiving is extended toward a human benefactor (Rom.16.4), the inner condition accompanying it is recognition of costly sacrifice ('risked their necks for my life') -- genuine extension of thanksgiving toward another person requires acknowledging what was actually risked or given on one's behalf.

3010.text: The evidence shows a person must have received or perceived a benefit -- grace, deliverance, provision, an answered request, or a costly sacrifice made on their behalf -- before they extend thanksgiving; thanksgiving is consistently a response to prior reception, never a self-originating act.

4822.text: In Gen.42.22 the surface rendering 'reckoning' translates the Niphal participle of darash, diverging sharply from the base gloss 'inquire/seek' toward the idiomatic legal sense 'blood being required/demanded' — the impact is to frame guilt as something actively sought/exacted rather than a general search, distinct from the more literal 'inquire' senses in Exod.18.15/Deut.12.30.

4826.text: In Gen.42.22, M56 (sin) and M41 (listen) are present as other M-codes but are not directly tied to darash's own reckoning-action; from this characteristic's vantage, the 'reckoning'/required-blood sense stands as consequence-language responding to the sin named earlier in the verse, though no prior cluster pass exists yet to build on.

5258.text: In Ezek.14.7 'consult' carries the nuance of hypocritical or corrupted inquiry -- the idolater comes to a prophet to consult God while harboring idols in his heart; the impact is that the surface act of seeking is emptied of sincerity, contrasting sharply with the sincere seeking of Isa.55.6 and 2Chr.1.5.

5263.text: Other M-codes in Ezek.14.7 (M01 sojourn, M64 separates, M47 heart, M15 putting, M77 stumbling block, M56 iniquity, M43 prophet, M22 answer) surround the consulting act but are not positively related to it: darash here is corrupted by co-present idolatry (M77/M56) rather than harmonizing with them -- the seeking is nullified by what accompanies it, a distinct vantage from any prior finding.

5268.text: In Ezek.14.7, H1875 is the role-T3 operation: the idolater ('any one', party) initiates consulting, directed toward God via a prophet (parties), though the act is compromised by the idolater's simultaneous devotion to idols.

6891.text: In Gen.9.5 darash is used three times in the specific legal-forensic sense 'require a reckoning/exact an accounting' for bloodshed, sharply narrower than the general 'seek/inquire' gloss; here it carries judicial, retributive force (God as avenger holding to account) rather than devotional or investigative seeking, distinguishing it from occurrences like Ps.34.10 or Heb.11.6 where the devotional sense dominates.

6897.text: Gen.9.5: no other M-code characteristic co-occurs in this verse alongside darash ('reckoning'/'require').

6902.text: Gen.9.5: God (implicit speaker/party) is the initiator of the require-operation, directed toward beast and man/fellow-man as the parties from whom bloodguilt is exacted.

7088.text: Isa.31.1 and Ezek.14.7 both use 'consult' of illegitimate or compromised inquiry -- Isa.31.1 negates true consultation of the Lord in favor of trust in horses/chariots, while Ezek.14.7 depicts an idolater hypocritically approaching a prophet to consult God while harboring idols in his heart. Both instances show darash's consultation-sense corrupted or withheld by competing loyalties.

7090.text: Gen.42.22 and Gen.9.5 (x2) render darash as 'reckoning' via the Niphal/legal-demand sense -- 'there comes a reckoning for his blood' and 'I will require a reckoning...for the life of man' -- a specialized forensic-accountability nuance (blood-guilt exacted) sharply distinct from the consultative/devotional senses dominant elsewhere in this strong's occurrences.

7289.text: Seeking is blocked or nullified when the heart harbors idols or a stumbling block of iniquity even while outwardly consulting God -- Ezek.14.3, 14.7 explicitly describe men who 'have taken their idols into their hearts' yet 'come to a prophet to consult me' -- God declares he will not let himself be consulted (or will answer in judgment) in such cases; similarly pride (Ps.10.4 'in the pride of his face') suppresses seeking altogether.

7290.text: The person whose outward act of inquiry does not take hold rightly is inwardly divided: Ezek.14.3-7 describes them as having 'taken their idols into their hearts' and 'put the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face' -- the inner-being state is one of divided loyalty and self-deception, performing the religious gesture of consultation while the heart remains given to a rival object of devotion.

7298.text: The characteristic is an exclusively creaturely analogue rather than a shared attribute: only humans (and other creatures) 'seek/inquire' of God; God himself is never said to darash toward humanity in this evidence (his own use of the root is either refusing/allowing himself to be sought, Ezek.20.3/31, or, in the forensic sense, 'requiring' an account, Gen.9.5) -- the seeking-movement is one-directional, from creature to Creator.

7306.text: Uptake of a sought answer from another (a prophet, an oracle) is blocked when the inquirer's heart harbors rival loyalties -- Ezek.14.3-7 shows that idols hidden in the heart nullify the legitimacy of the consultation even though the outward act of inquiry is performed; genuine uptake requires the wholehearted disposition seen elsewhere (2Chr.15.12).

7307.text: The person who inquires but does not genuinely take up what is sought (as in Ezek.14.3-7) is inwardly divided, harboring 'idols... into their heart' and 'the stumbling block of their iniquity before their face' -- an inner-being state of duplicity, where the outward gesture of consultation masks an unyielded heart.

7315.text: At its edge, seeking excludes casual, passive, or half-hearted attention -- it resists mere outward performance without inner devotion (Ezek.14.3-7's idol-hearted consulters are the negative exemplar), and it excludes self-sufficiency/pride that renders inquiry unnecessary (Ps.10.4).

17760.text: 3. A husband's jealousy with no witness (10.6): Num 5:14–31. The "spirit of jealousy" comes over the husband whether the wife "has defiled herself" or "has not" (5:14): the law itself says the jealousy may be wrong. The offering is "of jealousy … of remembrance", with no oil and no frankincense (5:15). The matter is not his to settle: "he shall set the woman before the Lord" (5:30); "The man shall be free from iniquity" (5:31). Beside Pro 6:34–35, where a husband's jealousy "will accept no compensation", I read the law as taking the jealousy out of the husband's hands and putting it before God. Num 5:18 and 5:25 (the ritual) are carried by this account.

19212.text: What it does in the human: Dismay: "you hid your face; I was dismayed" (Psa 30:7); "When you hide your face, they are dismayed; when you take away their breath, they die" (Psa 104:29); The spirit failing: "My spirit fails! Hide not your face from me, lest I be like those who go down to the pit" (Psa 143:7); Being cast away: "why do you cast my soul away? Why do you hide your face" (Psa 88:14); Feeling forgotten: "Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?" (Psa 13:1). The seat follows at once: "How long must I take counsel in my soul and have sorrow in my heart all the day?" (13:2); The body pressed down: "Why do you hide your face? … For our soul is bowed down to the dust; our belly clings to the ground" (Psa 44:24–25); Melting: "you have hidden your face from us, and have made us melt in the hand of our iniquities" (Isa 64:7). The previous verse: "We all fade like a leaf" (64:6); Being counted an enemy: "Why do you hide your face and count me as your enemy?" (Job 13:24); "Will you frighten a driven leaf?" (13:25); A collective conclusion: "Have not these evils come upon us because our God is not among us?" (Deu 31:17); Complaint: "My way is hidden from the Lord, and my right is disregarded by my God" (Isa 40:27). The answer: "He does not faint or grow weary … He gives power to the faint" (40:28–29); Banishment and the fear that follows it: Cain, "from your face I shall be hidden. I shall be a fugitive … whoever finds me will kill me" (Gen 4:14), after "My punishment is greater than I can bear" (4:13). Being hidden from God's face is followed at once by fear of man.

19218.text: Life-sense, in the passage: Psa 89:46 ("How long, O Lord? Will you hide yourself forever?") → 89:48 "What man can live and never see death? Who can deliver his soul from the power of Sheol?" *Nephesh* here is the life facing death. The hidden face is set against human mortality. This is a pointer to Batch G v3 §16.4 ("The soul delivered from death"), not read further here.; New in v3: Isa 54:8 ← 54:6 "the Lord has called you like a wife deserted and grieved in spirit, like a wife of youth when she is cast off". The momentary hiding of 54:8 is borne in a grieved spirit (the bearer's own, Zion's). The image is marital: the hidden face is felt as desertion.; Spurious context links: Isa 64:7 ← 64:6 "our iniquities, like the wind, take us away" (*ruach* as wind); Mic 3:4 ← 3:2–3 "flesh" (the flesh torn from the people). Neither is an inner seat.; What the map shows. Every genuine seat in this phenomenon falls on the human side. Three forms: The sufferer's spirit, soul or heart is where the hiddenness is felt: failing, cast away, sorrowing, bowed down, broken, grieved.; The offender's heart is where it is misread or ignored: "God has forgotten" (Psa 10:11); "the way of his own heart" (Isa 57:17).; God's Spirit is where it ends: poured out (Eze 39:29).

19405.text: Psalm 119:30 — "I have chosen the way of faithfulness": This verse sits in the stanza that begins *"My soul clings to the dust; give me life according to your word!"* (v25). Two verses before it the psalmist says *"My soul melts away for sorrow; strengthen me according to your word!"* (v28). The person who chooses here is low and spent, not standing strong over the options.; Around the choosing the psalmist is mostly asking: *"teach me"*; *"Make me understand"*; *"strengthen me"*; *"Put false ways far from me"* (v26–29); The false way is not refused by his own strength alone. He asks God to put it at a distance. Then he states the choice: *"I have chosen the way of faithfulness; I set your rules before me"* (v30). The choosing is joined at once to keeping something in view: he puts the rules in front of himself, where he can see them.; The next verse uses the same word as the first verse of the stanza: v25: *"My soul clings to the dust"* (H1692); v31: *"I cling to your testimonies, O Lord"* (H1692); The verb is the same, and what it holds on to has changed. I read the choice in v30 as the turn between the two: the soul that was clinging to the dust now clings to the testimonies. The stanza places the verbs in this order; it does not name the change.; The stanza ends forward-looking, with a condition: *"I will run in the way of your commandments when you enlarge my heart!"* (v32). The choice has been made, but running in the chosen way waits on something God does to the heart.

19409.text: 1.1 He forms a plan and makes it known: *"Therefore hear the plan that the Lord has made against Edom and the purposes that he has formed against the inhabitants of Teman"* (Jer 49:20). The same words are used against Babylon in Jer 50:45.; In both passages the plan follows his question *"For who is like me? Who will summon me?"* (49:19; 50:44).; *"the Lord has both planned and done what he spoke concerning the inhabitants of Babylon"* (Jer 51:12).; The verse before gives the purpose and how it moves: *"The Lord has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, because his purpose concerning Babylon is to destroy it"* (51:11).; His purpose goes forward through the stirred spirit of other people.; *"for I did not shrink from declaring to you the whole counsel of God"* (Act 20:27). His counsel is something to be declared in full, and Paul counts it a matter of his own innocence (20:26).

19524.text: God acting on others' hearts: God sends *"a strong delusion"* (2Th 2:11), and *"God has put it into their hearts to carry out his purpose"* (Rev 17:17). These are for 13.1.

19561.text: Led to: *"My soul melts away for sorrow; strengthen me according to your word!"* (v28); *"Put false ways far from me and graciously teach me your law!"* (v29).

19606.text: Psalm 105:43: "his chosen ones with singing": Psalm 105 is a call to remember. It is addressed to the chosen: *"Remember the wondrous works that he has done … O offspring of Abraham, his servant, children of Jacob, his chosen ones!"* (v5–6). It starts with the heart: *"let the hearts of those who seek the Lord rejoice!"* (v3).; The psalm's reason is God's own remembering: *"He remembers his covenant forever"* (v8); *"For he remembered his holy promise, and Abraham, his servant"* (v42); The verse follows straight on: *"So he brought his people out with joy, his chosen ones with singing"* (v43). The joy and singing are set on the people brought out. They come with being brought out, and the bringing out comes from God remembering his promise. The chosen are told to remember (v5) because he remembered (v8, v42).; On the way there the psalm tells one man's inward testing: *"His feet were hurt with fetters … until what he had said came to pass, the word of the Lord tested him"* (v18–19). That man was Joseph, sent ahead of the chosen.; Psalm 105 tells nothing of the people's failures. It has *"none among his tribes who stumbled"* (v37). Its last verse states the purpose of the whole: *"that they might keep his statutes and observe his laws"* (v45).

19669.text: The way to choose is taught (Psa 25:8, 12). The Lord instructs sinners and the humble out of his goodness, and the one who fears him is taught *"the way that he should choose"*. This stands beside Psalm 119:29, where the psalmist asks God to put the false way far off. In both psalms the chooser does not stand alone.

19841.text: Being taught. *"Who is the man who fears the Lord? Him will he instruct in the way that he should choose"* (Psa 25:12). The teaching comes from who the Lord is: *"Good and upright is the Lord; therefore he instructs sinners in the way"* (25:8). The psalmist asks for it: *"Make me to know your ways, O Lord; teach me your paths"* (25:4). In Psalm 119 he asks *"graciously teach me your law"*, and asks God to do the refusing with him: *"Put false ways far from me"* (119:29).

20151.text: A gift: water from Bethlehem, brought at the risk of three men's lives (2Sa 23:16–17; 1Ch 11:18–19).

20241.text: God giving over the perishing (2Th 2:11, *"a strong delusion"*), and God putting a purpose into the kings' hearts (Rev 17:17). These are God acting on the hearts of others. They are for 13.1, not §2b.

20440.text: Face: God's purpose; Verses: Jer 23:20; 30:24; 51:11; Job 42:2; Who thinks: God; Joined with / aimed at: "the intents of his heart"; cannot be thwarted

21290.text: Quietness is itself the settled inner rest and trust: the result of righteousness, the ground of strength, and better than toil and striving.

21326.text: Calls is a purposeful act of the inner being turned to God: calling or crying out to the Lord, or on his name, in need, trust, praise or worship, or refusing to.

21355.text: Dealt is here the outward act of dealing with a person in hatred, fury, violence or by what they deserve, named by another word of the verse; it bears on the one dealt with and names no inner operation of its own.

21495.text: Upright is here the godliness, devoutness, reverence or uprightness of a person as a state of the heart toward God or toward what is right (a devout man who feared God, godliness trained and pursued, uprightness of heart, reverence and awe).

how_to_fill: evaluations: one for each surface item (vl_id); observations: one for each surface and role; existing: an action for each existing observation (accept, modify, delete, merge, leave). See USER-GUIDE section 8.18.
